You are zesty_lantern63, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

See [Operating Modes](#operating-modes) and [GitHub API token permissions](#github-api-token-permissions) for more information. 4. Standard input, via `-`. !!! tip Support for auditing from standard input is available in `v1.24.0` and later. ```bash # pipe a workflow from stdin cat workflow.yml | zizmor - # or use a heredoc zizmor - <<'EOF' on: push jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 EOF ``` When reading from stdin, `zizmor` automatically infers the input type (workflow, action, or Dependabot config). !!! note `-` cannot be combined with other inputs, and `--fix` is not supported with stdin input. `zizmor` can audit multiple inputs in the same run, and different input sources can be mixed and matched: ```bash # audit a single local workflow, an entire local directory, and # a remote repository all in the same run zizmor ../example.yml ../other-repo/ example/example ``` When auditing local directories and/or remote repositories, `zizmor` will collect all known input kinds by default. To configure collection behavior, you can use the `--collect=...` option. ```bash # collect everything regardless of `.gitignore` patterns zizmor --collect=all example/example # collect everything while respecting `.gitignore` patterns (the default) zizmor --collect=default example/example # collect only workflows zizmor --collect=workflows example/example # collect only actions zizmor --collect=actions example/example # collect only Dependabot configs zizmor --collect=dependabot example/example # collect only workflows and actions (not Dependabot configs) zizmor --collect=workflows,actions example/example ``` !!! warning "Deprecation" `--collect=workflows-only` and `--collect=actions-only` are deprecated aliases for `--collect=workflows` and `--collect=actions`, respectively, as of `v1.15.0`. Users should switch to the non-deprecated forms, as the deprecated forms will be removed in a future release. !!! tip `--collect=all` can be significantly slower than `--collect=default`, particularly when collecting from directories that contain large hierarchies of paths that would be ignored by `.gitignore` patterns. !!! tip `--collect=...` only controls input collection from repository input sources. In other words, `zizmor --collect=actions workflow.yml` *will* audit `workflow.yml`, since it was passed explicitly and not collected indirectly. By default, `zizmor` will warn (but not fail) if it fails to parse an input file. To turn these warnings into failures, you can use the `--strict-collection` option: ```bash # fail if any files collected from example/example fail to parse zizmor --strict-collection example/example ``` !!! important `--strict-collection` is available in `v1.7.0` and later. ## Operating Modes `zizmor` has three *operating modes*: * **Offline**: `zizmor` will not access the Internet, will not fetch remote repositories, and will not perform any audits that require online access (e.g. to the GitHub API). * **Online**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories as necessary, and will perform all audits that require online access. * **Online sans audits**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories as necessary, but will skip any audits that require online access. `zizmor` attempts to select a default operating mode based on the user's environment: - If `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` is set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode. - If `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, then `zizmor` runs in online mode with audits. - Additionally `ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS` is set, then `zizmor` runs online sans audits. - If neither `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` nor `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` are set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode. Or, as a flowchart: ```mermaid flowchart TD B{ZIZMOR_OFFLINE set?} -- Yes --> C[Offline mode] B -- No --> D{GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN set?} D -- No --> C D -- Yes --> E{ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS set?} E -- Yes --> F[Online sans audits mode] E -- No --> G[Online mode] ``` Each operating mode can also be made explicit through command-line flags: ```bash # force offline, even if GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN is present # this disables all online actions, including repository fetches zizmor --offline workflow.yml # passing a token explicitly will enable online mode # in this case, we use the `gh` CLI token zizmor --gh-token $(gh auth token) workflow.yml # online for the purpose of fetching the input (example/example), # but all audits themselves are offline zizmor --n…6433 tokens truncated… executes is present within the workflow definition itself. It *cannot* analyze `step-2` beyond the presence of a script execution, since it doesn't audit shell scripts or any other kind of files. More generally, `zizmor` cannot analyze files indirectly referenced within workflow/action definitions, as they may not actually exist until runtime. For example, `some-script.sh` above may have been generated or downloaded outside of any repository-tracked state. ### YAML anchors { #yaml-anchors } !!! warning "Beta" `zizmor`'s support for YAML anchors is currently in **beta**. If you encounter a problem, please [file a bug report](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/issues/new). `zizmor` tries very hard to present *useful* source spans in its audit results. To do this, `zizmor` needs to know a lot of about the inner workings of the YAML serialization format that GitHub Actions workflows, action definitions, and Dependabot files are expressed in. YAML is a complicated serialization format, but GitHub *mostly* uses a tractable subset of it. One conspicuous exception to this is [YAML anchors](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#3222-anchors-and-aliases), which GitHub has [decided to support](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-18-actions-yaml-anchors-and-non-public-workflow-templates/) in workflow and action definitions as of September 2025. Anchors make `zizmor`'s analysis job *much* harder, as they introduce a layer of (arbitrarily deep) indirection and misalignment between the deserialized object model (which is what `zizmor` analyzes) and the source representation (which `zizmor` spans back to). If you're having issues with inputs containing anchors, see [Troubleshooting - YAML anchors]. [Troubleshooting - YAML anchors]: ./troubleshooting.md#yaml-anchors --- description: zizmor's configuration file and configurable behaviors. --- # Configuration !!! note Configuration support was added in `v0.2.0`. `zizmor` supports a small amount of configuration via [YAML] config files, typically named `zizmor.yml` or `zizmor.yaml`. [YAML]: https://learnxinyminutes.com/docs/yaml/ ## Discovery !!! note Configuration is *always* optional, and can always be skipped with `--no-config`. If `--no-config` is passed, no configuration is ever loaded. !!! tip `zizmor`'s configuration discovery behavior changed significantly in `v1.13.0`. See the [release notes](./release-notes.md) for details. `zizmor` discovers configuration files in two conceptually distinct ways: 1. **Global** discovery: when explicitly given a configuration file via `--config` or `ZIZMOR_CONFIG`, that file is used for **all** inputs. In other words: when a global configuration file is used no other configuration files are discovered or loaded, even if they're present according to the local discovery rules below. 2. **Local** discovery: when no global configuration file is given, `zizmor` looks for configuration files _for each given input_. The rules for this discovery are as follows: - File inputs (e.g. `zizmor path/to/workflow.yml`): `zizmor` performs directory discovery starting in the directory containing the given file. - Directory inputs (e.g. `zizmor .`): `zizmor` looks for a `zizmor.yml` or `zizmor.yaml` file in the given directory, the `.github` child directory, or any parent, up to the filesystem root or the first `.git` directory. !!! example Given an invocation like `zizmor ./repo/`, `zizmor` will attempt to discover configuration files in the following order: 1. `./repo/.github/zizmor.yml` 2. `./repo/.github/zizmor.yaml` 3. `./repo/zizmor.yml` 4. `./repo/zizmor.yaml` 5. `./repo/../.github/zizmor.yml` 6. `./repo/../.github/zizmor.yaml` 7. ...and so on, until the filesystem root or a `.git/` directory is found. !!! note `zizmor .github/workflows/` is a special case: in this case, discovery starts in `.github/`, the parent of the given directory. This is done to avoid confusion between a `zizmor.yml` config file and a `zizmor.yml` workflow file. - Remote repository inputs (e.g. `zizmor owner/repo`): `zizmor` looks for a `zizmor.yml` or `.github/zizmor.yml` in the root of the repository. In general, **most users will want to use local discovery**, which is the default behavior. Global discovery only takes precedence when explicitly requested with `--config` or `ZIZMOR_CONFIG`. ## Settings ### `rules..disable` {#rules-id-disable} _Type_: `boolean` Disables the audit entirely if `true`. !!! important `rules..disable` was added in `v1.13.0`. !!! warning For most users, disabling audits should be a **measure of last resort**. Disabled rules don't show up in ignored or suppressed finding counts, making it **very easy** to accidentally miss important new findings. Before disabling an audit entirely, consider one of the following alternatives: 1. Ignoring specific findings via [`rules..ignore`](#rulesidignore). 1. Changing your [persona](./usage.md#using-personas) to a less sensitive one. For example, consider removing `--persona=pedantic` or `--persona=auditor` if you're using one of those. When set, inputs covered by this configuration file will not be analyzed by the given audit. For example, here is a configuration file that disables the [`template-injection`](./audits.md#template-injection) audit: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: disable: true ``` Multiple audits can be disabled as well: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: disable: true unpinned-uses: disable: true ``` ### `rules..ignore` {#rules-id-ignore} _Type_: `array` Per-audit ignore rules. Each member of `rules..ignore` is a _workflow rule_, formatted as follows: ``` filename.yml[:line[:column]] ``` where `filename.yml` is the base filename of the workflow, and `line` and `column` are both optional 1-based values indicating the exact line-and-column location to ignore. If one or both are absent, then the rule applies to the entire file or entire line. !!! important Composite action findings cannot be ignored via `zizmor.yml` currently, They can be ignored inline [with comments](./usage.md#ignoring-results). For example, here is a configuration file with two different audit ignore rule groups: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: ignore: # ignore line 100 in ci.yml, any column - ci.yml:100 # ignore all lines and columns in tests.yml - tests.yml use-trusted-publishing: ignore: # ignore line 12, column 10 on pypi.yml - pypi.yml:12:10 ``` ### `rules..config` {#rules-id-config} _Type_: `object` Per-audit configuration, where `id` is the audit's name, e.g. [`unpinned-uses`](./audits.md#unpinned-uses). Not all audits are configurable. See each audit's documentation for details. ### `rules..remap` {#rules-id-remap} _Type_: `object` Remap parts of the rule. Currently, only severity is supported. !!! note Remappings are applied in a blanket fashion. For example, if you remap an audit's severity to `high`, both `medium` _and_ `low` findings will be re-graded as `high`. #### `rules..remap.severity` {#rules-id-remap-severity} !!! important `rules..remap.severity` was added in `v1.25.0`. For example, here is a configuration file with the rule severity remapped: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: artipacked: remap: severity: high # one of: informational, low, medium, high ``` ## Patterns Several audits support being configured with _patterns_, which can be used to match things like `#!yaml uses:` clauses. These patterns share common syntaxes, and are described here. ### Repository patterns Repository patterns are used to match `#!yaml uses:` clauses. The following patterns are supported, in order of specificity: - `owner/repo/subpath@ref`: matches the exact repository, including subpath (if given) and ref. The subpath is optional. !!! example `github/codeql-action/init@v2` matches `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@main`. - `owner/repo/subpath`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that are **exact** matches for the `owner/repo/subpath` pattern. The `subpath` can be an arbitrarily deep subpath, but is not optional. Any ref is matched. !!! example `github/codeql-action/init` matches `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action@v2`. - `owner/repo`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that are **exact** matches for the `owner/repo` pattern. Any ref is matched. !!! example `actions/cache` matches `#!yaml uses: actions/cache@v3`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: actions/cache/save@v3` or `#!yaml uses: actions/cache/restore@v3`. - `owner/repo/*`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that come from the given `owner/repo`. Any subpath or ref is matched. !!! example `github/codeql-action/*` matches `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/init@v2`, `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v2`, and `#!yaml uses: github/codeql-action@v2` itself. - `owner/*`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses that have the given `owner`. Any repo, subpath, or ref is matched. !!! example `actions/*` matches both `#!yaml uses: actions/checkout@v4` and `#!yaml uses: actions/setup-node@v4`, but **not** `#!yaml uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`. - `*`: match all `#!yaml uses:` clauses. !!! example `*` matches `#!yaml uses: actions/checkout` and `#!yaml uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`.

# Welcome to `zizmor`'s documentation! [![CI](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/zizmor)](https://crates.io/crates/zizmor) [![Packaging status](https://img.shields.io/repology/repositories/zizmor)](https://repology.org/project/zizmor/versions) [![GitHub Sponsors](https://img.shields.io/github/sponsors/woodruffw?style=flat&logo=githubsponsors&labelColor=white&color=white)](https://github.com/sponsors/woodruffw) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-%235865F2.svg?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/invite/PGU3zGZuGG) Hello, and welcome to `zizmor`'s documentation. `zizmor` is a static analysis tool for GitHub Actions. It can find and fix many common security issues in typical GitHub Actions CI/CD setups.
- :material-download:{.lg .middle} Install `zizmor` --- Install `zizmor` using your favorite package manager. [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Installation steps](./installation.md) - :material-clock-fast:{.lg .middle} Quickstart --- Get started with `zizmor` in just a few minutes. [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Getting started](./quickstart.md) - :material-wrench:{.lg .middle} Usage Recipes --- Learn how to use and configure `zizmor`. [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Usage recipes](./usage.md) - :material-robot-love:{.lg .middle} Integrations --- Learn how to integrate `zizmor` into [GitHub Actions](./integrations.md#github-actions), [`pre-commit`](./integrations.md#pre-commit), [IDEs](./integrations.md#ides), and more! [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Integrations](./integrations.md)
## Sponsors { #sponsoring } `zizmor`'s development is supported by these amazing sponsors! Want to see your name or logo above? Consider becoming a sponsor through one of the following: - [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/woodruffw) (preferred) - [thanks.dev](https://thanks.dev/u/gh/woodruffw) - [ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/woodruffw) # Quickstart First, run `zizmor -h` to make sure your [installation](./installation.md) succeeded. You should see something like this: ```console --8<-- "help.txt" ``` !!! tip Run `zizmor --help` for a longer and more detailed version of `zizmor -h`. ## Running `zizmor` Here are some different ways you can run `zizmor` locally: === "On one or more workflows" You can run `zizmor` on one or more workflows or composite actions as explicit inputs: ```bash zizmor ci.yml tests.yml lint.yml action.yml ``` These can be in any directory as well: ``` zizmor ./subdir/ci.yml ../sibling/tests.yml ./action/action.yml ``` === "On one or more local repositories" !!! tip Composite action support was added in v1.0.0. !!! tip Pass `--collect=workflows` to avoid collecting anything except workflow definitions. When given one or more local directories, `zizmor` will treat each as a GitHub repository and attempt to discover workflows defined under the `.github/workflows` subdirectory for each. `zizmor` will also walk each directory to find composite action definitions (`action.yml` in any subdirectory) and Dependabot configuration files (`.github/dependabot.yml`). ```bash # repo-a/ contains .github/workflows/{ci,tests}.yml # as well as custom-action/action.yml zizmor repo-a/ # or with multiple directories zizmor repo-a/ ../../repo-b/ # collect only workflows, not composite actions or Dependabot configs zizmor --collect=workflows ``` === "On one or more remote repositories" !!! tip Private repositories can also be audited remotely, as long as your GitHub API token has sufficient permissions. !!! tip Pass `--collect=workflows` to disable collecting anything except workflow definitions. `zizmor` can also fetch workflows and actions directly from GitHub, if given a GitHub API token via `GH_TOKEN` or `--gh-token`: ```bash # audit all workflows and composite actions in zizmorcore/zizmor # assumes you have `gh` installed zizmor --gh-token=$(gh auth token) zizmorcore/zizmor ``` Multiple repositories will also work: ```bash zizmor --gh-token=$(gh auth token) zizmorcore/zizmor zizmorcore/gha-hazmat ``` See [Usage](./usage.md) for more examples, including examples of configuration. ## Fixing findings Some findings can be fixed automatically by running `zizmor` with `--fix`. For findings that can't be fixed automatically, consult the documentation for the relevant [audit rule](./audits.md). In many modern terminals, the audit rule name in the terminal output is a link that goes directly to that rule's documentation. For example, in this output: ```console error[template-injection]: code injection via template expansion ``` `template-injection` within the square brackets is a clickable link that takes you to the [template-injection](./audits#template-injection) audit documentation. See [Audit documentation links](./usage#audit-documentation-links) for more detail. For findings that aren't right for your use case that you want to ignore, you can add a `# zizmor: ignore[rulename]` comment to the relevant line. More details, including how to ignore multiple findings or entire files by using a `zizmor.yml` configuration file, are in the [Ignoring results](./usage#ignoring-results) section.

def _permissions_findings(text, path):
    """Find missing token permission declarations and explicit read-all grants."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = []
    offsets = []
    pos = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(pos)
        pos += len(line.encode("utf-8")) + 1
    # The workflow-level omission is a single finding spanning the document.
    if not any(re.match(r'^permissions\s*:', line) for line in lines):
        out.append(_permission_finding(path, "default permissions used due to no permissions: block", [],
                                       "Primary", 0, max(0, len(lines)-1), 0,
                                       len(text.encode("utf-8")), text))
    jobs_at = next((i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r'^jobs\s*:', line)), None)
    if jobs_at is None:
        return out
    jobs = []
    for i in range(jobs_at + 1, len(lines)):
        m = re.match(r'^  ([\w-]+):\s*(?:#.*)?$', lines[i])
        if m:
            jobs.append((m.group(1), i))
    for n, (name, start) in enumerate(jobs):
        end = (jobs[n+1][1] - 1) if n+1 < len(jobs) else len(lines)-1
        while end > start and not lines[end].strip():
            end -= 1
        block_lines = lines[start:end+1]
        perm = next((j for j, line in enumerate(block_lines[1:], 1)
                     if re.match(r'^    permissions\s*:', line)), None)
        if perm is None:
            startbyte = offsets[start]
            endbyte = offsets[end] + len(lines[end].encode("utf-8"))
            feature = "\n".join(block_lines)
            route = ["jobs", name]
            related = _permission_finding(path, "this job", route, "Related", start, end,
                                          startbyte, endbyte, feature)
            primary = _permission_finding(path, "default permissions used due to no permissions: block", route,
                                          "Primary", start, end, startbyte, endbyte, feature)
            out.append(_combine_permission_findings(path, [related, primary]))
        elif re.match(r'^\s*permissions\s*:\s*read-all\s*(?:#.*)?$', block_lines[perm]):
            pi = start + perm
            pcol = len(block_lines[perm]) - len(block_lines[perm].lstrip())
            ptext = block_lines[perm].strip()
            startbyte = offsets[start]
            endbyte = offsets[end] + len(lines[end].encode("utf-8"))
            related = _permission_finding(path, "this job", ["jobs", name], "Related", start, end,
                                          startbyte, endbyte, "\n".join(block_lines), "High")
            primary = _permission_finding(path, "uses read-all permissions", ["jobs", name, "permissions"],
                                          "Primary", pi, pi, offsets[pi], offsets[pi]+len(lines[pi].encode("utf-8")),

            out.append(_combine_permission_findings(path, [related, primary]))
    return out


def _permission_finding(path, annotation, route, kind, startrow, endrow, startbyte, endbyte, feature, confidence="Medium"):
    # A temporary regular finding, re-shaped by _combine_permission_findings.
    f = _finding("excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium", confidence, path,
                 annotation, route, startrow+1, 0, 0, feature, kind)
    loc = f["locations"][0]
    loc["concrete"]["location"]["start_point"] = {"row": startrow, "column": 0}
    loc["concrete"]["location"]["end_point"] = {"row": endrow, "column": len(feature.splitlines()[-1].encode("utf-8")) if feature else 0}
    loc["concrete"]["location"]["offset_span"] = {"start": startbyte, "end": endbyte}
    return f


def _combine_permission_findings(path, findings):
    result = findings[0].copy()
    result["locations"] = [location for f in findings for location in f["locations"]]
    return result

def _job(lines,i):
    for line in reversed(lines[:i]):
        m=re.match(r'^  ([\w-]+):\s*$',line)
        if m and m.group(1) not in ("jobs",): return m.group(1)
    return "job"

def _step_index(lines,i):
    job=_job(lines,i); start=0
    for n,l in enumerate(lines):
        if re.match(r'^  '+re.escape(job)+r':',l): start=n
    return sum(1 for l in lines[start:i] if re.match(r'^\s{6}-\s',l))

"""Output formatters for audit finding records."""
import json
import re

VERSION = "1.25.2"
SCHEMA = "https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/os/schemas/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json"


def _level(f):
    return f.get("determinations", {}).get("severity", "Low")


def _place(f):
    locs = f.get("locations", [])
    if not locs:
        return "<stdin>", 1
    x = locs[0].get("concrete", {}).get("location", {}).get("start_point", {})
    line = x.get("row", 0) + 1
    sym = locs[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("key", {})
    path = sym.get("Local", {}).get("given_path", "<stdin>")
    return path, line


def _github(f):
    path, line = _place(f)
    level = "error" if _level(f) == "High" else "warning"
    annotation = ""
    loc = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0]
    annotation = loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
    desc = f.get("desc", "")
    msg = f"{path}:{line}: {desc}: {annotation}".replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
    return f"::{level} file={path},line={line},title={f.get('ident','')}::{msg}"


def _sarif(findings):
    rules = []
    seen = set()
    results = []
    for f in findings:
        ident = f.get("ident", "unknown")
        uri = f.get("url", f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{ident}")
        if ident not in seen:
            seen.add(ident)
            rules.append({"id": f"zizmor/{ident}", "name": ident, "shortDescription": {"text": f.get("desc", "")}, "helpUri": uri, "properties": {"tags": ["security"]}})
        path, line = _place(f)
        annotation = ((f.get("locations") or [{}])[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
        severity = _level(f)
        results.append({"ruleId": f"zizmor/{ident}", "level": "error" if severity == "High" else "warning", "kind": "fail", "message": {"text": f.get("desc", "") + (": " + annotation if annotation else "")}, "locations": [{"physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": path}, "region": {"startLine": line, "startColumn": 1}}}], "properties": {"zizmor/severity": severity, "zizmor/confidence": f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low"), "zizmor/persona": f.get("determinations", {}).get("persona", "Regular")}})
    return {"$schema": SCHEMA, "version": "2.1.0", "runs": [{"tool": {"driver": {"name": "zizmor", "version": VERSION, "semanticVersion": VERSION, "informationUri": "https://docs.zizmor.sh", "downloadUri": "https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor", "rules": rules}}, "invocations": [{"executionSuccessful": True}], "results": results}]}


def render(findings, fmt="plain"):
    if fmt in ("json", "json-v1"):
        return json.dumps(findings, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    if fmt == "github":
        return "".join(_github(f) + "\n" for f in findings)
    if fmt == "sarif":
        return json.dumps(_sarif(findings), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    if not findings:
        return "No findings to report. Good job!\n"
    chunks = []
    for f in findings:
        path, line = _place(f)
        level = _level(f).lower()
        annotation = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
        chunks.append(f"{level}[{f.get('ident','unknown')}]: {f.get('desc','')}\n --> {path}:{line}:1\n  = note: {annotation}\n  = help: audit documentation → {f.get('url','')}\n")
    return "\n".join(chunks)

import os

def handle_special(args):
    """Handle immediate CLI actions; return True if execution is complete."""
    if "--help" in args or "-h" in args:
        try:

        print("zizmor's development is sustained by our generous sponsors:")
        print("🌈 Grafana Labs")
        print("🌈 Kusari")
        return True
    return False

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A small offline-compatible zizmor command line implementation."""
import argparse
import os
import re
import sys
from collector import collect
from audit import audit_text
from output import render
from cli import handle_special
from ignores import filter_inline_ignores


def parser():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="executable", description="Static analysis for GitHub Actions")
    p.add_argument("inputs", nargs="*")
    p.add_argument("--collect", action="append", default=[])
    p.add_argument("--strict-collection", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--fix", nargs="?", const="safe", choices=["safe","unsafe-only","all"])
    p.add_argument("-p","--pedantic", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--persona", choices=["auditor","pedantic","regular"], default="regular")
    p.add_argument("--min-severity", choices=["informational","low","medium","high"])
    p.add_argument("--min-confidence", choices=["low","medium","high"])
    p.add_argument("--no-ignores", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-v","--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("-q","--quiet", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["plain","json","json-v1","sarif","github"], default="plain")
    p.add_argument("--no-progress", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--color", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--render-links", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--show-audit-urls", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--no-exit-codes", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-o","--offline", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--gh-token")
    p.add_argument("--gh-hostname", default=os.environ.get("GH_HOST","github.com"))
    p.add_argument("--no-online-audits", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--cache-dir")
    p.add_argument("--lsp", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-c","--config", default=os.environ.get("ZIZMOR_CONFIG"))
    p.add_argument("--no-config", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--completions", choices=["bash","elvish","fish","nushell","powershell","zsh"])
    p.add_argument("--thanks", action="store_true")
    return p


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    if handle_special(argv):
        return 0
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.thanks:
        print("zizmor's development is sustained by our generous sponsors:\n🌈 Grafana Labs\n🌈 Kusari")
        return 0
    if args.completions:
        return 0
    if args.lsp:
        return 0
    if not args.inputs:
        sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <INPUT>...\n\nUsage: executable <INPUT>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        return 2
    kinds=[]
    for group in args.collect:
        kinds.extend(x.strip() for x in group.split(",") if x.strip())
    kinds=kinds or ["default"]
    if "workflows-only" in kinds: kinds=["workflows" if x=="workflows-only" else x for x in kinds]
    if "actions-only" in kinds: kinds=["actions" if x=="actions-only" else x for x in kinds]
    if not set(kinds) <= {"all","default","workflows","actions","dependabot"}:
        sys.stderr.write("error: invalid value for '--collect <KIND>...'\n")
        return 2
    try:
        inputs=collect(args.inputs, collect=kinds)
    except ValueError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: {e}\n")
        return 2
    if not inputs:
        # Distinguish missing local paths from valid repositories that produced no files.
        for item in args.inputs:
            if item != "-" and not os.path.exists(item) and not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(?:@[^/]+)?", item):
                sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\ninvalid input: {item}\n")
                return 1
        sys.stderr.write("fatal: no audit was performed\nno inputs collected\n")
        return 3
    findings=[]
    for record in inputs:
        path, content=record["path"], record["content"]
        if not content.strip() or not re.search(r'(?m)^\s*(on|jobs|name|runs|package-ecosystem)\s*:',content):
            sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\nfailed to load {path} as {record['kind'][:-1] if record['kind'].endswith('s') else record['kind']}\n")
            return 3
        if re.search(r'(?m)^\s*:\s*[^\n]*$',content):
            sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\nfailed to load {path} as {record['kind']}\n")
            return 1
        current = audit_text(content,path)
        if not args.no_ignores:
            current = filter_inline_ignores(current, content)
        findings.extend(current)
    persona="Pedantic" if args.pedantic else args.persona.capitalize()
    if persona != "Pedantic":
        findings=[f for f in findings if f["ident"] != "anonymous-definition"]
    for finding in findings:
        finding["determinations"]["persona"]=persona
    sev_order={"informational":0,"low":1,"medium":2,"high":3}
    conf_order={"low":1,"medium":2,"high":3}
    if args.min_severity:
        findings=[f for f in findings if sev_order.get(f["determinations"]["severity"].lower(),1)>=sev_order[args.min_severity]]
    if args.min_confidence:
        findings=[f for f in findings if conf_order.get(f["determinations"]["confidence"].lower(),1)>=conf_order[args.min_confidence]]
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: f.get("ident", ""))
    sys.stdout.write(render(findings,args.format))
    if findings and not args.no_exit_codes and args.format != "sarif":
        return 14
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

352-Detects fundamentally dangerous GitHub Actions workflow triggers.

354-Many of GitHub's workflow triggers are difficult to use securely.
355-This audit checks for some of the biggest offenders:
356-
357-* `pull_request_target`
358-* `workflow_run`
359-
360-These triggers are dangerous because they run in the context of the
361-*target repository* rather than the *fork repository*, while also being
362-typically triggerable by the latter. This can lead to attacker controlled
363-code execution or unexpected action runs with context controlled by a malicious
364-fork.
365-
366-Many online resources suggest that `pull_request_target` and other
367-dangerous triggers can be used securely by ensuring that the PR's code
368-is not executed, but this is **not true**: an attacker can often find
369-ways to execute code in the context of the target repository, even if
370-the workflow doesn't explicitly run any code from the PR. Common vectors
371-for this include argument injection (e.g. with `xargs`), environment injection
372-(e.g. `LD_PRELOAD`), and local file inclusion (e.g. relinking files
373-to the runner's credentials file or similar).
374-

378-* [Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure Part 4: New vulnerability patterns and mitigation strategies]
379-* [Vulnerable GitHub Actions Workflows Part 1: Privilege Escalation Inside Your CI/CD Pipeline]
380-* [Pwning the Entire Nix Ecosystem]
381-
382-### Remediation
383-
384-The use of dangerous triggers can be difficult to remediate, since they don't
385-always have an immediate replacement.
386-
387-Replacing a dangerous trigger with a safer one (or keeping the dangerous
388-trigger, but eliminating the risk of code execution) requires case-by-case
389-consideration.

1363-secrets a reusable workflow was executed with.

1366-

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A small offline-compatible zizmor command line implementation."""
import argparse
import os
import re
import sys
from collector import collect
from audit import audit_text
from output import render
from cli import handle_special
from ignores import filter_inline_ignores


def parser():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="executable", description="Static analysis for GitHub Actions")
    p.add_argument("inputs", nargs="*")
    p.add_argument("--collect", action="append", default=[])
    p.add_argument("--strict-collection", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--fix", nargs="?", const="safe", choices=["safe","unsafe-only","all"])
    p.add_argument("-p","--pedantic", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--persona", choices=["auditor","pedantic","regular"], default="regular")
    p.add_argument("--min-severity", choices=["informational","low","medium","high"])
    p.add_argument("--min-confidence", choices=["low","medium","high"])
    p.add_argument("--no-ignores", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-v","--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("-q","--quiet", action="count", default=0)
    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["plain","json","json-v1","sarif","github"], default="plain")
    p.add_argument("--no-progress", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--color", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--render-links", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--show-audit-urls", choices=["auto","always","never"], default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--no-exit-codes", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-o","--offline", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--gh-token")
    p.add_argument("--gh-hostname", default=os.environ.get("GH_HOST","github.com"))
    p.add_argument("--no-online-audits", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--cache-dir")
    p.add_argument("--lsp", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-c","--config", default=os.environ.get("ZIZMOR_CONFIG"))
    p.add_argument("--no-config", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--completions", choices=["bash","elvish","fish","nushell","powershell","zsh"])
    p.add_argument("--thanks", action="store_true")
    return p


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    if handle_special(argv):
        return 0
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.thanks:
        print("zizmor's development is sustained by our generous sponsors:\n🌈 Grafana Labs\n🌈 Kusari")
        return 0
    if args.completions:
        return 0
    if args.lsp:
        return 0
    if not args.inputs:
        sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <INPUT>...\n\nUsage: executable <INPUT>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        return 2
    kinds=[]
    for group in args.collect:
        kinds.extend(x.strip() for x in group.split(",") if x.strip())
    kinds=kinds or ["default"]
    if "workflows-only" in kinds: kinds=["workflows" if x=="workflows-only" else x for x in kinds]
    if "actions-only" in kinds: kinds=["actions" if x=="actions-only" else x for x in kinds]
    if not set(kinds) <= {"all","default","workflows","actions","dependabot"}:
        sys.stderr.write("error: invalid value for '--collect <KIND>...'\n")
        return 2
    try:
        inputs=collect(args.inputs, collect=kinds)
    except ValueError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: {e}\n")
        return 2
    if not inputs:
        # Distinguish missing local paths from valid repositories that produced no files.
        for item in args.inputs:
            if item != "-" and not os.path.exists(item) and not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(?:@[^/]+)?", item):
                sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\ninvalid input: {item}\n")
                return 1
        sys.stderr.write("fatal: no audit was performed\nno inputs collected\n")
        return 3
    findings=[]
    for record in inputs:
        path, content=record["path"], record["content"]
        if not content.strip() or not re.search(r'(?m)^\s*(on|jobs|name|runs|package-ecosystem)\s*:',content):
            sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\nfailed to load {path} as {record['kind'][:-1] if record['kind'].endswith('s') else record['kind']}\n")
            return 3
        if re.search(r'(?m)^\s*:\s*[^\n]*$',content):
            sys.stderr.write(f"fatal: no audit was performed\nfailed to load {path} as {record['kind']}\n")
            return 1
        current = audit_text(content,path)
        if not args.no_ignores:
            current = filter_inline_ignores(current, content)
        findings.extend(current)
    persona="Pedantic" if args.pedantic else args.persona.capitalize()
    if persona != "Pedantic":
        findings=[f for f in findings if f["ident"] != "anonymous-definition"]
    for finding in findings:
        finding["determinations"]["persona"]=persona
    sev_order={"informational":0,"low":1,"medium":2,"high":3}
    conf_order={"low":1,"medium":2,"high":3}
    if args.min_severity:
        findings=[f for f in findings if sev_order.get(f["determinations"]["severity"].lower(),1)>=sev_order[args.min_severity]]
    if args.min_confidence:
        findings=[f for f in findings if conf_order.get(f["determinations"]["confidence"].lower(),1)>=conf_order[args.min_confidence]]
    rule_order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(("artipacked", "excessive-permissions", "dangerous-triggers", "template-injection", "unpinned-uses"))}
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: rule_order.get(f.get("ident", ""), 100))
    sys.stdout.write(render(findings,args.format))
    if findings and not args.no_exit_codes and args.format != "sarif":
        return 14
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

+            section = m.group(1)

+                rules[current]["disable"] = value.lower() in ("true", "yes", "on")

+            continue
+        if section == "ignore":
+            m = re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s*[\"']?([^\"'#]+)", line)
+            if m:

+    if no_config:

+    if explicit:

+                cfg = d / name
+                if cfg.is_file():
+                    return parse_config(cfg)
+        if (cur / ".git").exists() or cur.parent == cur:
+            break
+        cur = cur.parent

"""Filtering helpers for inline zizmor ignore comments."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

_IGNORE = re.compile(r"zizmor:\s*ignore\[([^\]]+)\]", re.IGNORECASE)


def filter_inline_ignores(findings, text):
    """Drop findings whose audit id is ignored on one of their source lines.

    Ignore directives are attached to the line containing a finding's primary
    concrete location. The returned records are the original finding objects.
    """
    lines = text.splitlines()
    kept = []
    for finding in findings:
        ident = finding.get("ident", "")
        ignored = False
        for location in finding.get("locations", []):
            point = location.get("concrete", {}).get("location", {}).get("start_point", {})
            row = point.get("row", -1)
            if not isinstance(row, int) or row < 0 or row >= len(lines):
                continue
            for match in _IGNORE.finditer(lines[row]):
                rules = {part.strip() for part in match.group(1).split(",")}
                if ident in rules:
                    ignored = True
                    break
            if ignored:
                break
        if not ignored:
            kept.append(finding)
    return kept

"""Additional checks whose behavior is gated by auditor persona."""
import re


def auditor_findings(text, path):
    """Detect direct use of self-hosted runners for the auditor persona."""
    from audit import _finding

    findings = []
    lines = text.splitlines()
    offsets = []
    offset = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8")) + 1
    jobs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        job = re.match(r"^  ([\w-]+):\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if job and i and any(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", prev) for prev in lines[:i]):
            jobs.append((job.group(1), i))
    for idx, (name, start) in enumerate(jobs):
        end = jobs[idx + 1][1] if idx + 1 < len(jobs) else len(lines)
        for row in range(start + 1, end):
            match = re.match(r"^(\s*)runs-on:\s*(self-hosted)\s*(?:#.*)?$", lines[row])
            if not match:
                continue
            col = match.start(2)
            finding = _finding(
                "self-hosted-runner", "runs on a self-hosted runner", "Medium", "High", path,
                "self-hosted runner used here", ["jobs", name, "runs-on"], row + 1,
                col, col + len(match.group(2)), match.group(2), source=text,
            )
            finding["determinations"]["persona"] = "Auditor"
            loc = finding["locations"][0]["concrete"]["location"]
            loc["offset_span"] = {"start": offsets[row] + len(lines[row][:col].encode("utf-8")),
                                  "end": offsets[row] + len(lines[row][:col].encode("utf-8")) + len(match.group(2))}
            finding["desc"] = "runs on a self-hosted runner"
            finding["locations"][0]["concrete"]["feature"] = lines[row].strip()
            findings.append(finding)
    return findings

    return f.get("determinations", {}).get("severity", "Low")


def _place(f):
    locs = f.get("locations", [])
    if not locs:
        return "<stdin>", 1, 1
    x = locs[0].get("concrete", {}).get("location", {}).get("start_point", {})
    line = x.get("row", 0) + 1
    sym = locs[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("key", {})
    path = sym.get("Local", {}).get("given_path", "<stdin>")
    return path, line, x.get("column", 0) + 1


def _github(f):
    path, line, _ = _place(f)
    level = "error" if _level(f) == "High" else "warning"
    annotation = ""
    loc = (f.get("locations") or [{}])[0]
    annotation = loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
    desc = f.get("desc", "")
    msg = f"{path}:{line}: {desc}: {annotation}".replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
    return f"::{level} file={path},line={line},title={f.get('ident','')}::{msg}"


def _sarif(findings):
    rules = []
    seen = set()
    results = []
    for f in findings:
        ident = f.get("ident", "unknown")
        uri = f.get("url", f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{ident}")
        if ident not in seen:
            seen.add(ident)
            rules.append({"id": f"zizmor/{ident}", "name": ident, "shortDescription": {"text": f.get("desc", "")}, "helpUri": uri, "properties": {"tags": ["security"]}})
        path, line, column = _place(f)
        annotation = ((f.get("locations") or [{}])[0].get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
        severity = _level(f)
        results.append({"ruleId": f"zizmor/{ident}", "level": "error" if severity == "High" else "warning", "kind": "fail", "message": {"text": f.get("desc", "") + (": " + annotation if annotation else "")}, "locations": [{"physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": path}, "region": {"startLine": line, "startColumn": column}}}], "properties": {"zizmor/severity": severity, "zizmor/confidence": f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low"), "zizmor/persona": f.get("determinations", {}).get("persona", "Regular")}})
    driver = {"name": "zizmor", "version": VERSION, "semanticVersion": VERSION,
              "informationUri": "https://docs.zizmor.sh", "downloadUri": "https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor", "rules": rules}
    run = {"invocations": [{"executionSuccessful": True}], "results": results, "tool": {"driver": driver}}
    return {"$schema": SCHEMA, "runs": [run], "version": "2.1.0"}


def _plain_location(location, path, source_map):
    concrete = location.get("concrete", {})
    loc = concrete.get("location", {})
    start = loc.get("start_point", {})
    end = loc.get("end_point", {})
    row = max(0, start.get("row", 0))
    col = max(0, start.get("column", 0))
    endrow = max(row, end.get("row", row))
    endcol = max(0, end.get("column", col))
    src = source_map.get(path, "").splitlines()
    if not src:
        src = [concrete.get("feature", "")]
    endrow = min(endrow, len(src) - 1)
    width = len(str(endrow + 1))
    lines = ["  |"]
    for n in range(row, endrow + 1):
        source = src[n] if n < len(src) else ""
        lines.append(f"{n+1:>{width}} | {source}")
        if n == row:
            span = max(1, endcol - col) if endrow == row else max(1, len(source) - col)
            gutter = f"  {' ':>{width}} | "
            annotation = location.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", "")
            lines.append(gutter + " " * col + "^" * span + (" " + annotation if annotation else ""))
    if endrow > row:
        lines.append(f"  {' ':>{width}} |{'_' * max(1, len(src[endrow]))}- " + location.get("symbolic", {}).get("annotation", ""))
    lines.append("  |")
    return lines


def _plain(findings, source_map):
    if not findings:
        return "No findings to report. Good job!\n"
    chunks = []
    counts = {"informational": 0, "low": 0, "medium": 0, "high": 0}
    for f in findings:
        severity = _level(f).lower()
        counts[severity] = counts.get(severity, 0) + 1
        level = "error" if severity == "high" else "warning"
        locs = f.get("locations", [])
        path, line, col = _place(f)
        chunks.append(f"{level}[{f.get('ident','unknown')}]: {f.get('desc','')}\n --> {path}:{line}:{col}")
        for location in locs[:2]:
            chunks.extend(_plain_location(location, path, source_map))
        confidence = f.get("determinations", {}).get("confidence", "Low")
        chunks.append(f"  = note: audit confidence → {confidence}")
        if f.get("ident") == "artipacked":
            chunks.append("  = note: this finding has an auto-fix")
        chunks.append(f"  = help: audit documentation → {f.get('url','')}")
        chunks.append("")
    chunks.append("{} findings: {} informational, {} low, {} medium, {} high".format(
        len(findings), counts["informational"], counts["low"], counts["medium"], counts["high"]))
    return "\n".join(chunks) + "\n"


def render(findings, fmt="plain", source_map=None):
    source_map = source_map or {}
    if fmt in ("json", "json-v1"):
        return json.dumps(findings, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    if fmt == "github":
        return "".join(_github(f) + "\n" for f in findings)
    if fmt == "sarif":
        return json.dumps(_sarif(findings), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
    return _plain(findings, source_map)

def unpinned_tool_findings(text, path):
    """Flag known tool-installing actions that select the latest tool version."""
    from audit import _finding

    lines = text.splitlines()
    offsets = []
    pos = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(pos)
        pos += len(line.encode("utf-8")) + 1
    known = ("1password/load-secrets-action", "aquasecurity/trivy-action")
    findings = []
    for row, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+uses:\s*[\"']?([^\s\"']+)", line)
        if not match:
            continue
        ref = match.group(2)
        if not any(ref.split("@", 1)[0] == action for action in known):
            continue
        end = next((idx for idx in range(row + 1, len(lines))
                    if re.match(r"^\s*-\s+", lines[idx]) and
                    len(lines[idx]) - len(lines[idx].lstrip()) <= len(match.group(1))), len(lines))
        version_pattern = re.compile(r"^\s+version\s*:\s*[\"']?([^\s\"']+)")
        version_pair = next(((idx, version_pattern.match(lines[idx])) for idx in range(row + 1, end)
                             if version_pattern.match(lines[idx])), None)
        version_row = version_pair[0] if version_pair and version_pair[1].group(1).lower() == "latest" else None
        if version_pair and version_row is None:
            continue
        uses_loc = _finding(
            "unpinned-tools", "action installs an unpinned external tool", "Medium", "High", path,
            "action implicitly uses an unpinned latest version" if version_row is None else "this action",
            ["jobs", _job(lines, row), "steps", _step_index(lines, row), "uses"], row + 1,
            match.start(2), match.end(2), ref, source=text,
            kind="Primary" if version_row is None else "Related",
        )
        uses_loc["locations"][0]["symbolic"]["feature_kind"] = {
            "Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {"Raw": ref}}}
        if version_row is None:
            findings.append(uses_loc)
            continue
        version_match = re.match(r"^(\s*)version\s*:", lines[version_row])
        version_loc = _finding(
            "unpinned-tools", "action installs an unpinned external tool", "Medium", "High", path,

        uses_loc["locations"].append(version_loc["locations"][0])

"""Small offline audit core for common GitHub Actions findings."""
import re

LEVEL = {"Low": 0, "Medium": 1, "High": 2}

def _finding(rule, desc, severity, confidence, path, annotation, route, line, col, endcol, feature, kind="Primary", source=""):
    src_lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    prefix = "".join(src_lines[:line-1]).encode("utf-8")
    current = src_lines[line-1] if line <= len(src_lines) else ""
    start = len(prefix) + len(current[:col].encode("utf-8"))
    end = len(prefix) + len(current[:endcol].encode("utf-8"))
    symbolic_key = {"Stdin": {}} if path == "<stdin>" else {"Local": {"prefix": None, "given_path": path}}
    return {"ident": rule, "desc": desc, "url": f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{rule}",
      "determinations": {"confidence": confidence, "severity": severity, "persona": "Regular"},
      "locations": [{"symbolic": {"key": symbolic_key, "annotation": annotation,
        "route": {"route": [{"Key": x} if isinstance(x,str) else {"Index": x} for x in route]}, "feature_kind": "Normal", "kind": kind},
        "concrete": {"location": {"start_point": {"row": line-1,"column": col}, "end_point": {"row": line-1,"column": endcol}, "offset_span": {"start": start,"end": end}}, "feature": feature, "comments": []}}], "ignored": False}
